ตลาดหลักทรัพย์แห่งประเทศไทย (ตลท.) และสภาธุรกิจตลาดทุนไทย (FETCO) ร่วมคณะรัฐบาลไทยเดินทางโรดโชว์ตลาดทุน ณ นครนิวยอร์ก สหรัฐอเมริกา และกรุงลอนดอน สหราชอาณาจักร ระหว่างวันที่…

general.title: น้ำท่วมกรุงเทพอ่วม เปิดชื่อโรงเรียนดัง กทม. ได้รับผลกระทบ สถานการณ์อุทกภัย

general.summary_original:
BANGKOK — 28 September 2026, The Transport Co., Ltd. (BKS) said that passenger vans and minibuses on 13 routes have temporarily suspended services due to severe flooding that has made roads impassable.

BKS said it was closely monitoring heavy rain and flooding across the country, particularly on routes in the eastern region, where several areas have been affected.

Operators of BKS-affiliated passenger vans and minibuses have temporarily suspended services on the following 13 routes:

  1. Route 46: Bangkok (Ekkamai) – Rayong
  2. Route 56: Bangkok (Ekkamai) – Phanom Sarakham
  3. Route 914: Bangkok (Ekkamai) – Chanthaburi
  4. Route 917: Bangkok (Ekkamai) – Laem Ngop
  5. Route 9916: Bangkok (Ekkamai) – Kabin Buri – Rong Kluea Market
  6. Route 12: Bangkok (Chatuchak) – Lop Buri
  7. Route 21: Bangkok (Chatuchak) – Nakhon Ratchasima
  8. Route 35: Bangkok (Chatuchak) – Map Ta Phut – Rayong
  9. Route 915: Bangkok (Chatuchak) – Ban Khai – Laem Mae Phim
  10. Route 921: Bangkok (Chatuchak) – Ongkharak – Rong Kluea Market
  11. Route 9907: Bangkok (Chatuchak) – Chanthaburi
  12. Route 9908: Bangkok (Chatuchak) – Trat
  13. Route 9920: Bangkok (Chatuchak) – Ban Sang – Prachin Buri

BKS said it had instructed affiliated operators to continue monitoring conditions and assess the safety of each route before resuming normal services.

The company is also closely monitoring flooding and traffic conditions across its network and coordinating with relevant agencies and operators. Any changes to services will be announced to the public.

BKS said passenger safety remained its top priority and that it would adjust services according to conditions to minimise disruption to travellers.

general.title_original: Puripol shares Asian 200m record after Asian Games gold
general.summary_original:
28 September 2026, World Athletics has confirmed that Thai sprinter Puripol Boonsan’s 19.88-second run in the men’s 200m at the 2026 Asian Games is an Asian record, jointly held with Chinese sprinter Xie Zhenye.

Puripol, who won gold in the event, clocked 19.88 seconds with a tailwind of -3.0 metres per second.

Xie recorded the same time of 19.88 seconds at a competition in London on 21 July 2019, with a legal tailwind of +0.9 metres per second. World Athletics regulations allow a tailwind of up to +2.0 metres per second for a performance to qualify for record purposes.

Despite sharing the Asian record, Puripol continues to hold the Asian Games records in both the men’s 100m and 200m.

His Asian Games records stand at 9.90 seconds in the 100m and 19.80 seconds in the 200m.

general.title_original: GULF Volunteers Join Forces to Support Bangkok’s Flood-Affected Communities, delivering ‘GULF Care’ Relief Kits and Essential Supplies
general.summary_original:
In response to flooding across several areas of Bangkok, Gulf Development Public Company Limited (GULF), led by Mr. Sitamon Ratanavadi, Head of Corporate Social Responsibility, brought together ‘GULF Volunteers’ also known as ‘GULF Asa’, comprising employees from GULF’s head office and power plants across the Group, to lend a helping hand to flood-affected communities in Bangkok. The volunteers worked together to pack 650 ‘GULF Care’ relief kits, containing essential supplies to help ease the hardship of those affected.

Each relief kit contains essential items, including boxed milk, canned food, instant noodles, and basic medicines. GULF also provided 6,000 bottles of drinking water for distribution to flood-affected communities across Bangkok. The relief supplies were presented to Assoc. Prof. Dr. Tavida Kamolvej, Deputy Governor of Bangkok, who received them on behalf of the Bangkok Metropolitan Administration at Bangkok City Hall 2.

GULF remains committed to standing alongside communities affected by flooding and will continue to support relief and recovery efforts across the country, helping communities overcome the crisis and return to their daily lives as soon as possible.
